verdicts.quote: The tool should provide a summary dashboard within the app showing top recurring themes (e.g., “3 notes on agitation post-2am”) and a heat map of note frequency by hour and nurse
This summary will be generated by an Azure Function that analyzes the Azure SQL notes table every 10 minutes and stores aggregated insights in a read-only
The system allows a note to be edited by its author until the next Logic App sync, then locks it.

The author can view their own edit history. - The charge nurse can view the edit history. - The original content is preserved in the audit trail. - Every edit creates a new version in Azure SQL with VersionId, PreviousContent, EditTimestamp, and EditorId. - The charge nurse can view the edit history via a dropdown in the UI. - The spreadsheet reflects only the latest version. - View History lists all versions with timestamp, editor ID and content - Versions are sorted chronologically and the latest version is highlighted

The “Pending Action” tag is replaced with “Escalated” when a charge nurse updates the note status. The original tag is preserved in the audit log along with the timestamp and the user ID of the charge nurse who made the change.

The charge nurse can re-escalate the note if the original author does not resolve it within 24 hours of escalation. The system will track the escalation timestamp and trigger a reminder via Azure Logic Apps

The system should display a client-side validation error: “Patient must be selected before saving.” This message appears inline beneath the patient selection dropdown with a red border and icon. The save button is disabled until a valid patient is selected, and the error is not sent to the server

The spreadsheet will show the updated content from the 08:00 edit, as the sync at 08:15 pulls the latest version from Azure SQL. If the author opens “View History” afterward, they will see a list of all versions
